standard_prerequisites: The cap operation with a first Chern class and the description of the latter through divisors of meromorphic sections
Flat pullback of cycles with multiplicities along the irreducible components of the fibre, and rational equivalence for locally finite sums of cycles
The prepare version of the formula: the flat pullback of the divisor of a meromorphic section is the multiplicity weighted sum of the restrictions to the components
core_obligations: Write the cycle as a finite linear combination of classes of integral closed subspaces
Reduce to a single integral closed subspace: it suffices to produce a rational equivalence on the preimage of that subspace, because the locally finite sums then reassemble

Over that preimage, which is the fibre product with the subspace, decompose the flat pullback of the cycle according to the irreducible components of the fibre with their multiplicities, and note that the restriction of a meromorphic section to each component is again a nonzero meromorphic section

Apply the prepare version of the formula to identify the pullback of the divisor of the section with the multiplicity weighted sum, and conclude by observing that the two sides of the displayed identity in the statement are exactly the pushforwards of the two cycles so obtained
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the class of a single integral closed subspace and work on its preimage
Decompose the flat pullback into components with multiplicities and restrict the meromorphic section
Apply the prepare formula and read off the identity as the pushforward of a cycle on the preimage
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the compatibility of flat pullback with the cap by a first Chern class at source lines 2802-2813, label lemma-flat-pullback-cap-c1, whose proof occupies source lines 2815-2856. The proof reduces a general cycle to the class of a single integral closed subspace and then works on its preimage under the flat morphism, where the flat pullback of that class becomes a sum over the irreducible components of the fibre weighted by their multiplicities. The meromorphic section used to describe the Chern class is restricted to those components and the prepare version of the formula identifies the two cycles on the preimage, after which the two sides of the statement are recognised as the pushforwards of those cycles. The counted statement records neither the reduction to a single subspace nor the decomposition of the pullback with multiplicities.
